citation.title: Review protection of bank verification identifiers.

rules.detects: Finds an eleven-digit value within 128 scalar values of a BVN or bank-verification label, including labels after the value. Reports the value location at error severity.
rules.exceptionGuidance: Remove unnecessary personal data or mask it before use. Record a justified exception through the existing configuration if retention is necessary.
rules.limits: Literal keywords are ASCII case-insensitive substrings. Nearby labels provide context, not proof of assignment, data flow or an issued BVN. No public check-digit algorithm is assumed. Longer digit runs, repeated/sequential examples, dates, versions, hex and UUID fragments are excluded by the existing engine controls. Unlabelled identifiers and unsafe field handling are separate rules.
rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary identifiers from source and test data, use generated fixtures, and mask identifiers before logging. If retention is necessary, use the existing justified-exception configuration and review its scope.

rules.whyItMatters: Identification numbers linked to individuals require appropriate protection.

citation.title: Review protection of identifying email addresses.

rules.detects: Finds bounded ASCII email-shaped values at error severity using the existing example-domain validator. Reports the address location without copying the address into results.
rules.exceptionGuidance: Remove unnecessary personal data or mask it before use. Record a justified exception through the existing configuration if retention is necessary.
rules.limits: The local part is 1–64 ASCII letters, digits or dot, underscore, percent, plus and hyphen. The domain prefix is 1–64 letters, digits, hyphens or dots and ends in a dot plus a 2–24-letter suffix. This is a detection shape, not full RFC mailbox validation: quoted local parts, internationalised addresses and longer domains are unsupported, and punctuation within a shaped address can be permissive. The email boundary keeps the span inside a longer token: a match cannot start after a punctuation neighbour inside the local part (the oversized-local-part guard), while a sentence-ending dot after the domain does not reject a match. Reserved documentation domains and their subdomains are excluded; the existing synthetic .example corpus domain remains a positive. Public contact and role addresses still require contextual review.
rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary addresses from fixtures and configuration, replace them with generated test data, and mask addresses in diagnostics. Use the existing justified-exception configuration for deliberately retained public contacts.
rules.title: Email-address detection
rules.whyItMatters: An email address may identify an individual and need protection.
